task_description: Make the Continuum .ipa play every system the web PWA plays, plus PS1, on branch ps1-pcsx-rearmed. The iOS app currently ships one core (pcsx_rearmed) and a Library that lists .cue/.chd/.pbp/.iso; the web build already has four real cores as WASM (fceumm, mgba, genesis_plus_gx, snes9x). Build all five for aarch64-apple-ios as dylibs and wire them in so the .ipa can launch .nes, .sfc/.smc, .gba, .gb/.gbc, .sms, .md/.gen, .gg and PS1 content. Four parts: (1) generalise scripts/build-core.sh's Darwin-only PS1 path into a five-core iOS builder behind a NEW subcommand namespace (`ios <core>`, `ios-all`, `ios-names`), because a bare core name already means 'build it as WASM for the web' and overloading one would break the web build; (2) extend the iOS artefact chain (build-engine.sh stages and hard-fails on all five, project.yml embeds all five, package-ipa.sh's fallback covers all five, ios.yml asserts each one in the .ipa); (3) replace the single hardcoded PS1 declaration in ContinuumApp.swift with a five-core table plus one extension-to-core routing table that both the Library row and the launch path consult, with ensureCoreLoaded(coreId:) still reading engine.coreState fresh on every call; (4) document it in SESSION_HANDOFF.md. ABSOLUTE CONSTRAINTS: do not touch web/, do not modify crates/**, keep the WASM build green, keep every architectural invariant (import-and-copy with original filenames, no security-scoped URLs on the launch path, engine.coreState as the only source of truth, ensureCoreLoaded after stopSession, one MTLDevice owned by Rust, the picker configuration and its delegate lifetime machinery), no em dashes, a distinct HUD string on every failure path. Commit locally; do not push, do not open or modify a PR, do not trigger CI.

verification.semantic_review: v1 NEEDS_CHANGES (.agents/tasks/task-ios-all-cores/2026-09-18-054600-review.md), then addressed. The review confirmed all seven numbered requirements were met and found ten issues, of which four were substantive and are now fixed: (1) `ios-all` ran each core as a subshell used as an `if` condition, where bash disables errexit, so a failing make or cp fell through to the artefact check and could report a stale dylib as ok; each core now runs as a separate bash process, and the expected dylib is deleted before every build and every staging. (2) Nothing verified a staged dylib exported the libretro API, which is exactly what mgba's -force_load link over an LTO archive can get wrong; ios_stage_dylib now asserts nm -gU | grep -q retro_run for all five. (3) The BIOS HUD line stopped appearing at attach once nothing was loaded there, and its doc comment still claimed otherwise; declareAllCores now writes it and biosStatus names the core in all three branches. (4) The macOS job kept timeout-minutes: 60 while going from one native core build to five; raised to 120, and the XcodeGen step gained a conditional cmake install. Also adopted: the mgba CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_TARGET_TYPE workaround is now passed pre-emptively, the make dylib fallback is narrowed to *_libretro_ios.dylib, and build-engine.sh now checks the five names against project.yml, ios.yml and ContinuumApp.swift before compiling anything. Not adopted: an actions/cache step for .work/ios, because it adds CI behaviour the task did not ask for; it is recorded in SESSION_HANDOFF as the next lever and is safe now that a stale artefact cannot be mistaken for a fresh one.
verification.summary: Every Linux-verifiable gate passes. cargo test: 74 passing. cargo test --features native-core,uniffi-bindings: 84 passing (no Rust was touched; crates/** is untouched in the diff). cargo check --profile ios --target aarch64-apple-ios --features native-core,uniffi-bindings: clean. swiftc -frontend -parse on native/ios/ContinuumApp.swift and native/ios/MetalCanvas.swift: exit 0, which is a spell-check only (no iOS SDK here and the UniFFI facade is not generated), so the core table's types, the coreState Optional handling, List/ForEach identity and the extension routing were reviewed by eye and by a semantic review pass. bash -n on scripts/build-core.sh, native/ios/build-engine.sh and native/ios/package-ipa.sh: valid. yaml.safe_load on native/ios/project.yml and .github/workflows/ios.yml: valid, with all five dylibs asserted present as embed:true link:false codeSign:false dependencies, all five asserted in the .ipa verify step, and info.properties still holding UIFileSharingEnabled and LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace. plistlib.load on native/ios/Info.plist: valid, 20 keys. NAME TRACE: build-core.sh's ios_core_config defines each of the five canonical dylib names exactly once; build-engine.sh and package-ipa.sh hardcode none and read them from `build-core.sh ios-names`; project.yml, ios.yml and ContinuumApp.swift each carry all five spelled identically, and build-engine.sh now enforces that agreement on the runner before any core is compiled. WEB REGRESSION: a stubbed-copy harness proves bare `build-core.sh fceumm|mgba|genesis_plus_gx|snes9x|all` and no-args all still reach ensure_toolchain and build_core, `pcsx_rearmed` still routes to iOS, and nothing under web/ is modified. ROUTING: a scripted check proves the launchable extension set equals the routing table's key set and that .bin is importable but deliberately unroutable. Also verified empirically in this sandbox: that a subshell used as an `if` condition swallows a failure while a separate bash process does not, which is the basis for the ios-all fix. docker_build is skipped: this project has no Dockerfile, and the equivalent macOS work (five core dylib builds, xcodegen, xcodebuild, the .ipa) plus the on-device launch of each system cannot run in this Linux sandbox and are verified only by the orchestrator's CI run and device test afterward.
